Title: Mother, son killed in Temerloh tanker crash laid to rest
Article:
TEMERLOH: The remains of a mother and her 12-year-old son who died in a crash involving a tanker lorry and a car along Jalan Temerloh–Triang near Kampung Lebak last Friday were laid to rest at the Kampung Sanggang Muslim Cemetery here today.
Nur Fatima Syuhada Abdullah, 39, was buried beside her son, Muhammad Fattah Aisy Naufal Saifulnizam, 12, in a joint funeral after Friday prayers, with the burial completed at 2.30pm.
The sombre atmosphere turned emotional as the boy's father, Saifulnizam Sulaiman, 39, struggled to contain his grief as his wife and son were laid to rest.
The remains were earlier claimed by the family from the Forensic Medicine Unit of Sultan Ahmad Shah Hospital here at 10am.
Saifulnizam said the remains were prepared and shrouded at the hospital's forensic unit, before taken to Saidina Abu Bakar As Siddiq Mosque in Kampung Sanggang for funeral prayers.
"The remains were buried in my wife's hometown," he told reporters here today.
Saifulnizam said he last saw his wife and son on Tuesday before returning to Kampung Gadung, Sendayang, Negeri Sembilan, to manage his freshwater fish farming ponds.
He said he had been working on the fish-farming project since early this month and had been travelling between Jerantut and his hometown.
"We have fish ponds in Jerantut, and at the same time, I was expanding the farming project in my hometown in Sendayang, so I returned there alone last Tuesday.
"My wife and son left for Sendayang after Friday prayers and were supposed to arrive at 6pm.
"I had bought some organic tofu to serve them when they arrived, but they never made it because of the accident last Friday," he said.
In the 4pm incident last Friday, the mother and son died after the car they were travelling in was crushed by a tanker lorry carrying 32,000 litres of fuel.
The accident occurred when the tanker, travelling from Bera towards Temerloh, lost control, entered the opposite lane and crashed into the car.
Both vehicles caught fire, killing the mother and son.
The 37-year-old lorry driver suffered minor injuries and has been remanded until tomorrow. The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.

Title: GLCs, GLICs are public trust, not political property, says CSO Platform
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Government-linked companies (GLCs) and government-linked investment companies (GLICs) must be treated as institutions of public trust, not "political property", says the CSO Platform for Reform.
The coalition said lessons from the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into Lembaga Tabung Haji should extend beyond the pilgrims' fund to all state-linked entities entrusted with public assets and resources.
"GLCs and GLICs manage assets and resources of significant public interest. They must be governed as institutions of public trust, not as patronage networks or tokens for political allies," it said in a statement.
The coalition also criticised opposition MPs who walked out during the special Dewan Rakyat sitting to debate the RCI report, saying the move undermined Parliament's role in ensuring accountability.
The
RCI report
, declassified on July 29 and debated on Aug 11, exposed a massive asset-liability deficit at Tabung Haji, including the use of "creative accounting" to facilitate improper profit distributions and high-risk investments that resulted in billions of ringgit in losses.
According to the CSO Platform, seven investments suffered total losses, contributing to nearly RM13 billion in rescue and impairment costs that were largely absorbed through a government bailout involving Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd.
"The fund's accountability extends beyond its depositors and beneficiaries to all Malaysians, particularly since public funds were utilised to absorb these massive losses," it said.
The coalition also rejected suggestions that those raising concerns about Tabung Haji in the media should be questioned, saying transparency was essential when public funds were involved.
It called for firm action against anyone found responsible for mismanagement or negligence following a comprehensive investigation, and urged authorities to disclose the names, roles and specific findings involving those held accountable.
The CSO Platform also renewed its call for board and senior management appointments at GLCs and GLICs to be made through transparent, merit-based processes free from political influence.
It also urged stronger independent audits and oversight mechanisms to prevent a repeat of such institutional failures.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Alam Maritim fell to six-month low following MACC remand of CEO Azmi Ahmad
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Alam Maritim Resources Bhd fell to near six-month low today after its group managing director and group chief executive officer Datuk Azmi Ahmad was remanded by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to assist an ongoing investigation.
At 3.40pm, the counter fell three sen, or 11.54 per cent, to 23 sen, with 1.44 million shares changing hands, marking its highest trading volume in more than two months.
The stock has fallen about 23 per cent year-to-date, giving the company a market capitalisation of RM102.48 million at its current share price.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, offshore oil and gas services provider said the remand was to facilitate the ongoing investigation and does not constitute a finding of wrongdoing.
"The board has taken the necessary measures to ensure continuity of the group's operations and will make further announcements should there be any material development," it said.

Title: Singapore halts construction waste exports to Johor with immediate effect
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Singapore has halted all exports of construction and demolition (C&D) waste to Malaysia with immediate effect following concerns over alleged illegal dumping in Pontian.
Johor Solid Waste and Public Cleansing Management Corporation (SWCorp) director Zainal Fitri Ahmad said the decision was conveyed by Singapore's National Environment Agency (NEA) during a phone call today.
He said NEA group director for resource and sustainability Chan Chin Kai contacted him to discuss the export and disposal of C&D waste from the republic into Pontian.
During the call, Johor SWCorp emphasised that any waste export to Malaysia must strictly comply with existing laws and obtain prior approval from relevant local enforcement agencies.
"Johor SWCorp submitted a list of nine companies identified as being involved in exporting C&D waste from Singapore to the NEA to obtain further information and verification regarding their activities.
"The NEA informed us that shipments of C&D waste from Singapore to Malaysia will be halted with immediate effect, and further reviews will be conducted on the parties involved in Singapore," he said in a statement today.
Zainal Fitri said both agencies will maintain communication and share updates on investigation findings and follow-up actions.
He noted that the prompt response from the NEA is a positive step toward ensuring no further waste shipments enter Johor.
"As this involves two neighbouring countries, the NEA's quick response to issues raised by Johor residents and their immediate action are greatly appreciated," he said.
He added that the cooperation will strengthen Johor SWCorp's monitoring and enforcement efforts under the Solid Waste and Public Cleansing Management Act 2007 (Act 672).
The action by the NEA helps resolve a problem that residents in Mukim Sungai Karang, Pontian, claimed has persisted for nearly two years.
"Singapore has laws governing the export of used materials and waste products, while Malaysia also enforces strict regulations on waste management and disposal," Zainal Fitri said.
He revealed that Johor SWCorp has opened four investigation papers under Section 71(1) of Act 672, alongside an additional investigation paper opened for a separate case involving local waste disposal.
He stressed that SWCorp takes environmental contamination risks seriously, warning that unmonitored disposal could lead to dangerous materials being dumped alongside construction waste.
"Waste disposal must only take place at locations officially designated and permitted by law.
"Johor SWCorp will continue to step up monitoring and enforcement under Act 672 against any party carrying out illegal waste management or disposal in the state," he said.
It was previously reported that
construction waste
, believed to originate from demolished public housing flats in Singapore, was being dumped across several sites in Pontian over the past two years.
Residents claimed that the heavy vehicles travelled at night and into the early hours, with alleged dumping activities reported in Parit Sikom, Batu 26 Jeram Batu-Pengkalan Raja, Kampung Parit Rambai, Kampung Sungai Dinar and Mukim Sungai Karang.
They also claimed that the heavy vehicles had caused road hazards, with debris allegedly falling onto village roads and resulting in accidents involving motorcyclists.

Title: In Bangkok's gun district, traders say Thai crackdown misses the mark
Article:
LOAVES of sourdough bread now fill the display window of Suchart and Friends Gun, a firearms shop-turned-bakery in Bangkok's old quarter where pistols and rifles once lined the glass case.
Like all the gun shops in Thailand, it has been banned from importing firearms since a 2023 shooting at a Bangkok mall — one of several mass shootings, including at a school and a childcare centre, that have periodically prompted tighter regulation in a country with the second-highest private gun ownership in Asia.
Five months ago owner Warintorn Boonyachai decided to start baking bread to cover staff salaries, but would still like to see the gun-import ban lifted.
"I do still have hope, because like I've said, selling guns is less tiring than selling bread," said Warintorn, who also owns a baking school.
[[nid:1513096]]
That looks less likely after a 14-year-old gunman killed at least seven people in shootings at his home and school outside Bangkok this month, before fatally shooting himself.
In the wake of that shooting, Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul proposed a new law to suspend the issuance of new firearm purchasing permits and new gun ownership permits, and police were ordered to stop renewing permits for buying guns — measures that could further squeeze both sellers and prospective buyers out of the market.
In the capital's historic gun district, Thititorn Bupparamanee, president of the Firearms Traders Association of Thailand, said the suspension of permits would not fix the country's gun violence problem.
"They are not fixing the problem at the right places, because if they did, there would be less crime," he said, adding that the ban on the public purchasing legal guns through legal means may force some people to turn to the black market.
Thailand had ​an estimated 10.3 million firearms in civilian possession, equating to around 15 guns per 100 residents — the second-highest rate in Asia, behind Pakistan, according to a 2017 estimate by the Small Arms Survey.
Of those, a little more than six million were registered firearms, ​with another four million comprising unregistered weapons, the Geneva-based group estimated.
[[nid:1513095]]
The industry is worth about 2 billion baht (US$60.40 million), Thititorn said.
One gun store that has been in business for nearly seven decades had two guns left for sale and six staff, but they said the guns couldn't be sold and that new guns couldn't be imported.
Staff asked not to be named because they were not authorised to speak to media.
The mother of one 14-year-old student who fled the school shooting on Aug 7 said she supports the right to own guns, but wants to see more controls, including on people carrying weapons outside the home.
"There definitely should be a scrutiny everywhere on weapons, because knives are also as scary."
* The writers are from Reuters

Title: Carpenter in restaurant attack case sent for psychiatric assessment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A carpenter charged with causing grievous hurt to a businessman in a restaurant attack has been ordered to undergo a month-long
psychiatric assessment
at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta.
Sessions Court Judge Noridah Adam made the order last week following an application by defence lawyer Mohd Ruzaini Zulkifli on behalf of his client, Wong Weng Luen, 49.
Deputy public prosecutor Adiba Iman Hassan did not object to the application.
The court fixed Sept 17 for an update on the psychiatric assessment.
Ruzaini appeared with co-counsel Muhamad Firdaus Jumaludin during the mention.
Wong, along with technician Lai Kae Bin, 49, and memorial centre worker Wen Ken Fei, 30, has also applied to the High Court to review the Sessions Court's decision to deny them bail.
The hearing has been fixed for Aug 26.
The trio are currently being held at Sungai Buloh Hospital.
Lawyer Keith Moo, who is holding a watching brief for the victim, Andrew Teh, 47, said his client was still receiving treatment for injuries sustained in the attack.
Meanwhile, Kepong MP Lim Lip Eng said he would continue to monitor the case closely.
"The victim's safety, welfare and access to justice must remain our priority while the case proceeds in court," he said in a statement.
Wong, Lai and Wen are accused of voluntarily causing grievous hurt to Teh using dangerous weapons at Restoran Hing Kee Bakuteh in Jalan Kepong about 2am on May 7.
They were charged under Section 326 of the Penal Code, read with Section 34, which carries a jail term of up to 20 years and a fine or whipping upon conviction.
The attack allegedly stemmed from an incident in which Teh was accused of staring at a man believed to be intoxicated while dining at the restaurant.
Closed-circuit television footage of the several-minute assault later went viral on social media.
The footage showed Teh seated at a table before one of the men approached and began attacking him. Two others then joined in, initially appearing to restrain their friend before taking part in the assault.
Teh was punched, kicked and struck with various objects, including chairs and a kettle, before managing to escape.

Title: Iran blames US presence for Gulf waters pollution after oil spills
Article:
TEHERAN: Iran's foreign ministry on Monday blamed pollution in Gulf waters on US military operations in the region, after several oil spills were reported.
"This environmental damage stems from the US military presence and the wars it has waged in the region over the past five decades," foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told a news briefing.
"The damage caused to the environment of the Persian Gulf and the Sea of Oman is not solely linked to this war."
He called for the United States to be held accountable, estimating the damage at "trillions of dollars."
Last week, Iran called for compensation after an oil slick in the Strait of Hormuz reached the island of Qeshm, affecting beaches and an environmentally sensitive mangrove forest.
At the time, Baqaei cited preliminary evidence identifying "a foreign bulk carrier" as the source of the spill, which Iranian officials later said had been "completely cleaned up."
Earlier, Omani state media reported that an oil slick from a tanker that ran aground off Oman had reached the coastline.
An AFP investigation previously found that the vessel had been stranded for weeks near Oman's Al-Qibliyyah island after it was damaged by explosions.

Title: EPF contributions hit RM33.87bil in Q2 on higher membership, voluntary savings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Contributions to the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) rose 8.5 per cent year-on-year to RM33.87 billion in the second quarter of 2026 (2Q26), extending a strong upward trend in members' retirement savings.
The latest quarterly contribution continues the upward trend, from RM20.61 billion in Q2 2021; RM21.68 billion in Q2 2022; RM24.65 billion in Q2 2023; RM27.42 billion in Q2 2024 and RM31.21 billion in Q2 2025.
The continued growth in contributions and membership underscores the strengthening of EPF's contribution base, supported by steady employment growth, greater participation in voluntary savings and increased use of its digital platforms.
For the first half of 2026 (1H 2026), voluntary contributions reached RM14.15 billion, reflecting sustained participation in additional retirement savings.
"This reflects sustained member participation in voluntary savings, supported by EPF's digital platforms, which provide members with seamless and convenient access to make voluntary contributions," EPF said in a statement.
Malaysia's labour market also remained resilient, with the Statistics Department reporting an unemployment rate of 3.0 per cent in May 2026.
EPF said its membership base expanded strongly during the first half, with total members increasing 12.6 per cent year-on-year to 18.5 million.
New member registrations surged 52.9 per cent to 441,846 in 1H 2026 from 288,938 in the corresponding period last year.
Active membership grew even faster, rising 21.9 per cent to 10.95 million from 8.98 million previously, pointing to continued growth in formal employment and participation in the retirement savings system.
The number of active employers also increased 4.1 per cent to 645,207 from 619,662 a year earlier.
However, new employer registrations were broadly stable, edging down 0.4 per cent to 37,265 from 37,402 in 1H 2025.
EPF said participation in voluntary savings schemes also continued to strengthen.
Contributions under i-Saraan rose 15.7 per cent to RM1.33 billion, while the number of formal-sector members contributing above statutory rates through i-Topup increased 13.9 per cent year-on-year to nearly 204,450 in 1H 2026.
The continued growth in contributions and membership underscores the strengthening of EPF's contribution base, supported by steady employment growth, greater participation in voluntary savings and increased use of its digital platforms.

Title: Auku repeal offers chance to reset higher education, says UPM VC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The proposed abolition of the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (Auku) offers a timely chance to reset the country's higher education landscape, says Universiti Putra Malaysia vice-chancellor Datuk Professor Ahmad Farhan Mohd Sadullah.
He said the move should pave the way for greater autonomy for universities, with the Higher Education Ministry focusing on policy while institutions are given more room to manage their operations.
Such a shift, he said, could also help universities strengthen governance and achieve long-term financial sustainability.
"I welcome this move as it provides an opportunity to reset higher education.
"Areas that may be looked into would be greater autonomy but with higher accountability in governance to enable financial sustainability, and to change the Higher Education Ministry's role to a policy level, leaving universities to manage operations as part of their autonomy," he told the New Straits Times.
Farhan said the higher education landscape had changed considerably since the 1971 Act was introduced, with many of its provisions now requiring a rethink.
"With Auku being a very old Act, there will be many items that warrant an update, especially as higher education faces unprecedented new challenges," he said.
He said any new framework governing higher education must also give students greater opportunities to develop the skills and experience needed to become future nation-builders and leaders.
Farhan's comments came after Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the planned
abolition
of Auku, describing it as part of the government's broader push to accelerate reforms after initially prioritising political stability, national security and economic growth.
Other university leaders have also
welcomed
the move, describing it as an opportunity to strengthen institutional autonomy, governance and academic freedom.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: EPF's 1H26 investments income hits RM57.5bil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Employees Provident Fund (EPF) recorded a 48 per cent surge in investment income to RM57.5 billion for the first half of 2026 (1H 2026), driven by strong global equity markets and gains from its international portfolio.
Investment income for the second quarter alone rose 44 per cent to RM29.77 billion from RM20.61 billion in the corresponding period last year, with equities contributing RM20.94 billion, or 70 per cent of the quarterly total.
EPF chief executive officer Ahmad Zulqarnain Onn said the fund capitalised on the strong performance of global equity markets while maintaining a disciplined, long-term investment strategy.
"Similar to the first quarter, we continued to front-load income during the second quarter as market and geopolitical risks remain elevated.
"While equity markets have supported performance in the first half of the year, members should temper expectations, as such market opportunities may not repeat themselves in the second half of the year.
"Our focus remains on delivering sustainable long-term returns, backed by a resilient portfolio," he said in a statement.
The strong recovery in global equity markets during the quarter provided opportunities for EPF fund managers to realise gains, while easing concerns over energy prices and continued confidence in the artificial intelligence investment supercycle further supported investor sentiment.
Income from equities rose 52 per cent from RM13.77 billion in the second quarter of 2025 to RM20.94 billion in Q2 2026.
Fixed-income instruments contributed RM6.91 billion, accounting for 23 per cent of total investment income. Malaysian government securities and equivalents, loans and bonds continued to provide stable returns and served as a key defensive component of the portfolio amid market volatility.
Real estate and infrastructure generated RM1.30 billion, while money market instruments contributed RM0.62 billion, in line with expectations.
EPF's total investment assets stood at RM1.54 trillion as at June 30, with 39 per cent invested internationally.
International investments generated RM19.29 billion, accounting for 65 per cent of total investment income in the second quarter.
Investment income for Simpanan Konvensional and Simpanan Shariah amounted to RM24.16 billion and RM5.61 billion, respectively.
EPF said the investment income figures include unrealised mark-to-market gains and losses on securities, mainly arising from foreign exchange fluctuations. Consistent with previous years, these unrealised gains and losses are not distributable as dividends.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pickleball stars confirmed for Malaysia's first PPA Tour Asia event
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's top pickleball players will take on some of the world's leading professionals at the Leapmotor Kuala Lumpur Cup 2026, scheduled from Sept 9 to 13 at The Hood, Kuala Lumpur.
Organised as part of the Professional Pickleball Association Asia (PPA Asia) Tour, the tournament will bring international stars to Malaysia alongside the country's leading homegrown talent, giving fans the opportunity to watch world-class pickleball on home soil.
MALAYSIA'S TOP PLAYERS LEAD LOCAL CHALLENGE
Among the confirmed Malaysian players are:
Jimmy Liong (Kai Long)
Malaysia's highest-ranked international pickleball player, Jimmy Liong brings extensive experience competing on the world tour. He will lead the local challenge against some of the sport's biggest names.
Colin Wong
A familiar name on the Asian Tour, Colin Wong has built a reputation through his experience in competitive doubles. The local favourite will be looking to make an impact on home soil.
Syed Uzair Sufi
Syed Uzair Sufi brings experience from competing on the regional tournament circuit. He will be among Malaysia's representatives looking to make their mark at the tournament.
Timothy Foo
Rising Malaysian talent Timothy Foo will have the opportunity to test himself against some of the world's best players. The tournament will provide another major stage for the young player to gain international experience.
INTERNATIONAL STARS BRING WORLD-CLASS COMPETITION
Among the international players confirmed for the tournament are:
Gabriel Tardio (Bolivia)
Ranked No. 2 in the men's world rankings, Tardio is known for his explosive speed and energetic style of play.
Chao Yi Wang (Chinese Taipei)
The world No. 11 brings tactical precision, consistency and extensive experience on the international circuit.
Tama Shimabukuro (United States)
Ranked No. 14, Shimabukuro transitioned from competitive skateboarding to pickleball and has quickly risen through the world rankings.
Alix Truong (United States)
The world No. 14 is known for her court coverage and powerful backhand, making her one of the tournament's leading contenders.
Sahra Dennehy (Australia)
Ranked No. 21, Dennehy is one of Australia's leading tour professionals and brings strong all-round court coverage.
Danni-Elle Townsend (Australia)
The world No. 23 is a multiple-title winner known for her tactical baseline play and international experience.
FANS CAN WATCH THE ACTION LIVE
The Leapmotor Kuala Lumpur Cup 2026 will feature top local and international players competing from Sept 9 to 13 at The Hood, Kuala Lumpur.
Fans can watch the action in person, while those unable to attend can catch the tournament live on Tonton.

Title: Health Ministry creates 607 posts, approves RM1.57bil for Sabah healthcare
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The Health Ministry has created 607 new positions in Sabah as of Aug 1 this year to ensure state healthcare facilities operate at optimal capacity.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the new posts comprise 355 managerial and professional positions, including 77 specialist roles and 203 medical, dental, and pharmacy officers, as well as 252 implementation group positions.
He said this during a press conference after chairing the Sabah Health Development Joint Action Committee meeting here today, which was also attended by Sabah Women, Community Development and People's Wellbeing Minister Datuk Julita Mojungki.
Dzulkefly also announced that the federal government approved RM1.57 billion under the 13th Malaysia Plan Rolling Plan 1, covering 46 ongoing projects and seven new initiatives.
The new projects include the RM125 million
Sabah Heart Centre
and the RM81.95 million Type 5 Health Clinic with quarters in Sapulut, Nabawan.
He added that the ministry set a projected five per cent annual allocation growth target for the Sabah Health Department, which is expected to reach RM4 billion by 2030.
"In addition to long-term mega projects under MA63, the government remains committed to addressing the concerns of people at the grassroots level.
"Yesterday, I visited three district hospitals to assess urgent facility needs personally and approved almost RM4.3 million in immediate allocations overall," he said.
The ministry approved RM988,000 for Tambunan Hospital to upgrade its Emergency Department, repair a damaged canteen, and procure medical equipment.
A new hospital will also be built in Tambunan to replace the stalled Outpatient Department project, pending a preliminary works report from the Public Works Department.
In Ranau, RM1.279 million was approved, with RM950,000 allocated to rebuild the triage counter, repair the canteen, upgrade electrical transformer capacity for air conditioning, and procure three mortuary refrigerators.
Another RM329,000 will cover essential medical equipment and four new ambulances.
Dzulkefly noted that he and the ministry's secretary-general rejected the proposed site for a new Ranau Hospital, ordering an immediate feasibility study to refurbish the facility at its existing location instead.
For Kota Belud Hospital, RM2.01 million was approved to address its congested outpatient department, upgrade dental unit equipment, and procure a new mobile X-ray machine.

Title: Search teams comb rubble in Colombia nearly a week after quake as aid effort expands
Article:
BOGOTA: Search teams worked through the rubble of collapsed buildings in western Colombia on Sunday, nearly a week after a powerful earthquake devastated cities and towns across the country's west, killing hundreds and leaving many more missing, injured or homeless.
The 7.4-magnitude quake struck Monday morning in San Jose del Palmar, causing severe damage from the Pacific port of Buenaventura to Colombia's coffee-growing region and major western cities including Cali and Pereira.
Official estimates issued late on Saturday put the death toll at around 290, with 140 people still missing and nearly 4,000 injured.
More than two-thirds of the deaths were concentrated in Cali and Pereira, where apartment blocks, homes, churches, schools and hospitals were damaged or destroyed.
In Cali, Colombia's third-largest city, emergency workers continued searching unstable piles of concrete and twisted metal on Sunday as rescue efforts increasingly gave way to the recovery of bodies.
Aftershocks have added to the danger for crews working in damaged neighbourhoods and for residents still unable to return home.
[[nid:1513068]]
As hopes of finding more survivors dimmed, the relief operation was expanding.
In Bogota, the capital, a stadium has been turned into the country's biggest donation collection centre, with volunteers working around the clock to sort and load food, clothing, medicine and other basic supplies for affected areas.
Coordinating organisation Sencia said more than 7,000 volunteers had helped dispatch 700 tons of aid over five days.
In Pereira, authorities were also extending emergency help to injured pets and distributing donated animal food, underscoring the wider strain on families whose incomes and homes have been upended by the disaster.
The quake is the first major crisis facing President Abelardo De La Espriella, who took office just days before the disaster and now faces the task of overseeing relief and reconstruction.
De La Espriella said on Sunday that Colombian billionaire banker Jaime Gilinski, who also controls food company Nutresa , would donate 150 billion Colombian pesos (US$47.75 million) to rebuild hospitals and schools in Gilinski's hometown Cali.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: JDT's Sultan Ibrahim Stadium recreated with 400k Lego bricks
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: A Lego brick replica of the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, home of Johor Darul Ta'zim FC (JDT), was unveiled at Legoland Malaysia Resort yesterday.
The stadium model is the latest addition to Legoland's Miniland collection of Malaysian and regional landmarks.
The model was built using more than 400,000 Lego bricks and features animated crowd scenes, lighting effects and match-day elements modelled on the stadium.
Legoland Malaysia Resort vice-president CS Lim said the attraction showcased a modern Johor landmark and the state's football culture.
JDT chief operating officer Alistair Edwards said the
Sultan Ibrahim Stadium
represented Johor's ambition, unity and passion for football.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Muhyiddin graft trial: Nepturis got RM16.4mil for police HQ, court told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Construction company Nepturis Sdn Bhd received RM16.4 million from the government for the Klang North District Police Headquarters project in Selangor under the Jana Wibawa programme, the High Court heard today.
Selangor Public Works Department (PWD) director Lokman Nasir, 62, confirmed the payments after being shown government payment vouchers and payment instructions from the state PWD to Nepturis totalling RM141 million.
Nepturis is among companies linked to charges faced by former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin involving alleged abuse of power and money laundering over the Jana Wibawa programme.
Lokman, who retired on April 19, 2024, said in his witness statement that the RM16.4 million was paid through eight transactions between May 17, 2022, and Feb 3, 2023.
"I confirm that this project was under the Home Ministry and the financial allocation for this project came from the ministry.
"Besides that, there were several other payments that were still being processed or had not been made at the time," he said.
Under cross-examination by Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin, Lokman said there had been no non-compliance in the government payments.
Asked what he understood by non-compliance, he said it referred to any breach of the contract.
Wan Shaharuddin: "In this case, was there any non-compliance?"
Lokman: "So far, there was none."
The trial previously heard that Nepturis was asked to channel RM1 million to Bersatu in 2022 after securing the Klang North IPD project.
Nepturis managing director Mohd Rizman Akum Khan testified that he did not know the purpose of the payment, saying the cheque was issued on the instructions of company co-owner Lian Tian Chuan, better known as TC Lian.
He said he merely prepared the cheque without questioning the instruction.
Earlier, the prosecution informed the court that it wanted to amend the fourth charge against Muhyiddin to include KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd.
Judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin allowed the amendment after the defence raised no objection.
Under the first to fourth amended charges, the Pagoh MP faces four charges of using his position to obtain bribes totalling RM225.3 million in connection with Jana Wibawa projects involving Bukhary Equity Bhd, Nepturis, Mamfor Sdn Bhd, KCJ Engineering and Datuk Azman Yusoff for Bersatu.
For the fifth to seventh charges, Muhyiddin, as Bersatu president, is accused of receiving proceeds from unlawful activities totalling RM200 million, including RM200 million from Bukhary Equity, which was deposited into Bersatu's bank account.
KCJ, an engineering and construction company, is alleged to have contributed RM800,000 to Bersatu. It initially failed the Finance Ministry's assessment for the Jana Wibawa programme before eventually securing a RM62 million contract.
The trial before Noor Ruwena resumes tomorrow.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Caprice ordered to apologise, pay RM220,000 to Ebit Lew for defamation
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Rapper Caprice has been ordered to apologise and pay RM220,000 in damages to preacher Ebit Lew for defamation.
Sessions Court judge Zuhrina Mohamed Nor also ordered Caprice, whose real name is Ariz Ramli, 40, to remove seven statements made with Indonesian influencer Mondy Tattoo within 48 hours.
The court further restrained Caprice from making any future comments or statements concerning Ebit Lew, whose real name is Ebit Irawan Ibrahim Lew, 42.
Caprice's counterclaim was dismissed for lack of merit.
Ebit Lew had filed the suit over a video uploaded by Caprice on Sept 15, 2023, featuring Mondy, which he claimed contained defamatory allegations.
He said the video implied he had sexually harassed and taken advantage of Mondy, while portraying him as an irresponsible religious opportunist.
Ebit Lew claimed Caprice, as the first defendant, maliciously published the video without verifying the allegations with him or his legal team.
He also claimed the video had prompted numerous negative comments, insults and profanities from followers of Caprice's YouTube account.
Ebit Lew further claimed that defamatory statements made by Caprice and Mondy had resulted in him being criticised, ridiculed and humiliated.
On Sept 29, 2023, police called several individuals to assist in investigations into allegations of sexual harassment and defamation involving Ebit Lew, Mondy and Caprice.
Ebit Lew was represented by lawyer Datuk Akberdin Abdul Kader, while Caprice was represented by lawyer Mohd Rezan Ezra Muhammad Mosinal.
In a Facebook post following the judgment, Ebit expressed gratitude over the decision.
"Alhamdulillah, I am grateful to Allah. I won the suit against Caprice.
"He was ordered to apologise for the defamation and pay a total of RM220,000," he said.

Title: Azman: Anwar not seeking to strengthen Umno at DAP's expense
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is not seeking to strengthen Umno at the expense of DAP, said his political secretary and Federal Territories PKR chief Datuk Azman Abidin.
Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported Azman as saying that Anwar's close working relationship with Umno leaders should not be interpreted as an effort to strengthen the party or weaken DAP.
Azman said Anwar's role was to manage the multi-party unity government responsibly and work with all parties in the administration.
"So when the prime minister works with the Umno leadership, that doesn't mean that he is seeking to strengthen Umno's position and weaken DAP's.
"If some parties see the good relationship between the prime minister and Umno as a threat to DAP, I think that's more a question of political perception than political reality," he was quoted as saying.
Azman was responding to a claim by Kuala Lumpur DAP committee member Sangeet Kaur Deo that Anwar had divided Pakatan Harapan (PH) while empowering Umno.
Sangeet, daughter of the late former DAP chairman Karpal Singh, had called for DAP to remain in the unity government but reassess its relationship with Anwar.
https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/08/1512307/dap-veteran-leader-urges-party-speak-government-issues
She also accused Anwar of pitting PH component parties against one another while empowering Umno, and questioned why little action had been taken over what she described as attacks on DAP by Umno, despite both parties being part of the Federal administration.
Azman said criticism of Anwar and differing views among government parties were normal in a multi-party administration, but stressed that such differences needed to be managed carefully to protect the government's stability.
"If something can be resolved through negotiations, let's do that. If it needs to be brought to the cabinet, bring it to the cabinet.
"If there are policies that need improving, let's discuss and look for a solution.

Title: Thailand's second-quarter GDP grows 1.9pc year-on-year
Article:
BANGKOK: Thailand's economy grew 1.9 per cent in the second quarter of 2026 from a year earlier, official data showed yesterday, higher than the median forecast of 1.7 per cent in a Reuters poll of analysts.
On a seasonally adjusted quarterly basis, Southeast Asia's second-largest economy shrank 0.2 per cent in the April-June quarter, data from the National Economic and Social Development Council showed, a smaller fall than the poll forecast of a 0.6 per cent contraction.
In the January-March quarter, growth was 2.8 per cent on the year and a revised 0.6 per cent on the quarter. For the whole of 2026, the agency predicted the economy to grow 2.0 to 2.5 per cent, compared with a previous forecast of 1.5 to 2.5 per cent growth.
The economy expanded 2.4 per cent last year and has lagged regional peers since the Covid-19 pandemic, with high household debt restraining consumption.
The agency forecast that exports, a key driver of the economy, will increase 15.1 per cent this year, up from a previous forecast of a 9.6 per cent rise.
In the April-June quarter, the economy was weighed down by weak consumption due to high household debt and living costs.
In June, the central bank left its key interest rate unchanged at one per cent. The next monetary policy review is on Aug 26, and Bank of Thailand Governor Vitai Ratanakorn has said there was no need to raise interest rates for now. Reuters

Title: Bollywood stars told to drop surrogate ad in Indian state's food safety drive
Article:
NEW DELHI: Three top Bollywood actors, including Shah Rukh Khan, must stop appearing in surrogate advertisements of a brand mostly associated with a banned beetle nut product, India's Maharashtra state has said in a warning as it intensifies a food safety drive.
The new food safety chief of Maharashtra, home to Mumbai, has suspended licences of popular local restaurants as well as foreign outlets for poor hygiene, making him hugely popular on social media.
Last week, the state shut four Domino's stores and 12 warehouses of big grocery giants.
In a warning to Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn and Tiger Shroff, made public over the weekend, the state said the actors were promoting Vimal's cardamoms but the brand is associated largely with a prohibited beetle nut mix - called pan masala - sold in tiny 3.5 rupees (US$0.0366) packs and considered harmful, especially when mixed with tobacco.
Industry estimates show India's pan masala market was worth an estimated US$5 billion last year.
Health experts and doctors have said that is it a leading cause of oral fibrosis that often progresses to oral cancer.
Representatives of Khan, Devgn and Shroff did not respond to requests for comment, and neither did Vishnu & Company Trademarks, the company which owns the brand Vimal.
"Such use of the brand name and identity may have the effect of promoting, reinforcing or maintaining consumer recognition of the prohibited" product, the state Food and Drug Administration said in the notice, seeking an explanation from the actors within 15 days.
The Maharashtra authorities asked the three actors to remove the advertisements from their social media accounts, not cooperate with any further broadcast and provide details of their endorsement agreements with the manufacturer.
Surrogate advertisements have concerned Prime Minister Narendra Modi's federal government in the past, with the current regulatory regime often being disputed in courts.
The state in its notice to the actors said Indian law restricts advertisements that are misleading.
In one Vimal cardamom ad, the three actors appear in a festive celebration throwing saffron on one another. It has 106 million views on YouTube.
In 2024, Reuters reported, India was drafting stricter rules to bar surrogate ads  after complaints that liquor companies were promoting their brands using club glasses or music CDs.
The rules are yet to be finalised.

Title: Police deny drug cartel operating in Genting Highlands
Article:
KUANTAN: Pahang police have denied viral claims on social media that a large-scale drug cartel is operating unchecked in Genting Highlands, Bentong.
Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said police will investigate and act if any illegal activity is detected.
"If a police report involving illegal activity is lodged, we will immediately investigate and take appropriate action, regardless of the location," he said at the Pahang police headquarters today.
He was speaking to reporters after witnessing the handover of duties for the Pahang Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department chief post between Assistant Commissioner Muhammed Rizal Kamarudin and Senior Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Sukarno Mohd Zahar.
A recent post on Threads claimed that a major drug cartel was operating at the popular tourist destination and that no action had been taken despite multiple police reports.
On a separate matter, Azry Akmar said the tanker driver involved in a fatal crash that claimed two lives at Km9 of Jalan Temerloh-Triang near Kampung Lebak last Friday will be remanded until tomorrow.
"The investigation paper will be submitted to the deputy public prosecutor's Office today for further action," he said.
He said the 37-year-old driver is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing death by reckless or dangerous driving.
"The identities of both victims have been confirmed through DNA testing as Nur Fatima Abdullah, 39, and her 12-year-old son, Muhamad Fattah Aisy Nuafal Saifulnizam," he said.
It was reported that Nur Fatima and her son were burnt to death when their car caught fire after being hit by a tanker carrying 32,000 litres of diesel and petrol. The driver escaped with minor injuries.

Title: AmFIRST REIT's Q1 FY27 PAT more than double on higher occupancy, lower property expenses, finance costs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: AmFirst Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT) reported a 102.8 per cent increase in profit after tax to RM6.6 million for the first quarter ended June 30, 2026 (Q1 FY27), driven by higher occupancy, improved operating performance and lower finance costs.
Profit after tax rose RM3.4 million during the quarter from RM3.3 million a year earlier, while realised net income from operations increased 10 per cent to RM5.6 million from RM5.1 million.
Revenue from operations grew 7.5 per cent year on year (Y-o-Y) to RM27.2 million, supported by stronger rental and car park income, as well as higher contributions from its co-working space operations.
Overall portfolio occupancy improved to 88.3 per cent from 83.1 per cent a year earlier, reflecting stronger tenant take-up across several properties.
The stronger operating performance came despite the absence of RM1.7 million in one-off compensation income recognised in the corresponding quarter last year and the temporary closure of The Summit Hotel for a major rebranding and refurbishment exercise.
Property expenses fell 1.9 per cent to RM11.4 million, mainly due to lower repair and maintenance costs, higher electricity cost recoveries from tenants and a one-off electricity refund from Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB).
Finance costs also declined 3.3 per cent to RM8 million, with the average cost of borrowings falling to 4.09 per cent from 4.32 per cent a year earlier.
AmREIT Managers Sdn Bhd, the manager of AmFIRST REIT, said the higher occupancy and stronger revenue contributions, coupled with disciplined cost management, supported the improvement in realised net income.
The REIT manager said the results reflected stronger revenue contribution and effective cost optimisation, which enhanced the trust's overall operating performance.

Title: Kushner to hold talks with Netanyahu after rare meeting with Hamas
Article:
TEL AVIV: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is due to meet Donald Trump's envoy and son-in-law Jared Kushner on Monday, a day after he held a rare meeting with Hamas officials in Cairo, in a bid to push forward the US president's Gaza peace plan.
A diplomatic source said Hamas leader Khalil Al-Hayya was present at some of the meetings that mediators held with Kushner and Trump's Board of Peace envoy for Gaza, Nickolay Mladenov, in Cairo on Sunday.
It marks Kushner's second known meeting with representatives of Hamas, the Palestinian resistance group designated a terrorist movement by the United States.
Kushner previously met Hamas officials alongside US envoy Steve Witkoff in October 2025, helping clinch a deal that led to a ceasefire in Gaza and the release of remaining hostages seized by Hamas in the Oct 7, 2023 attacks on Israel.
Trump said in late July a deal was reached for the complete disarmament ‌of Hamas and other armed groups in Gaza.
But Netanyahu, who is seeking re-election at a vote due in October, has publicly rejected Trump's plan.
Trump had said the deal would be carried ​out in phases, with Israeli forces withdrawing from Gaza as disarmament ​proceeded and an International Stabilisation Force working with a new Palestinian police force to secure the enclave.
Hamas has said it agreed to the plan but the deal's implementation would depend on Israel first meeting its own commitments, including withdrawal and halting attacks.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: JB traffic dispersal plan being drawn up ahead of RTS Link operations
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Plans are being drawn up to ease traffic congestion in Johor Baru city centre and prevent new bottlenecks from emerging ahead of the launch of the Johor Baru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the plans involved coordination among agencies and integration of public transport systems, as travel patterns were expected to change, particularly around the city centre and areas directly connected to the system.
"This approach is in line with the aspiration for a more integrated, efficient, safe and people-friendly public transport system, particularly in supporting smoother cross-border mobility," he said in a statement after chairing the Cabinet Committee on Road Safety and Congestion (JK-MKKJR) meeting here today.
The RTS Link is scheduled to begin operations on Jan 1 next year and is expected to carry up to 10,000 passengers per hour in each direction.
The system will connect Bukit Chagar in Johor Baru with Woodlands North in Singapore.
On July 2, Transport Minister Anthony Loke told the Dewan Rakyat that the Federal Government would provide funding for the development of the Elevated Autonomous Rapid Transit (E-ART) project in Johor as part of efforts to address the congestion expected following the RTS Link's launch.
Loke also said the Transport Ministry (MoT), in collaboration with the Johor state government, was drawing up a traffic dispersal plan to strengthen the existing public transport system, including expanding the BAS.MY service network to 28 routes involving 254 buses, including electric buses.
He said under the Stage Bus Transformation Programme (SBST) 2.0, 157 buses would be allocated to routes serving Johor Baru Sentral and Bukit Chagar, with the service expected to begin early next year. — BERNAMA

Title: JHM eyes FY26 turnaround on automotive, semiconductor growth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: JHM Consolidation Bhd is set for a turnaround in financial year 2026 (FY26), driven by its core automotive lighting business, growth in its semiconductor-focused sheet metal division and an expected recovery in loss-making subsidiaries, according to RHB Research.
In a note, the firm expects the group's second quarter (Q2) of FY26 core earnings to improve quarter-on-quarter to between RM4 million and RM6 million, supported by a robust project pipeline, solid order books and more stable foreign exchange rates.
JHM's Q1 results marked a sharp reversal, with core profit after tax and minority interests (PATAMI) of RM2.3 million compared with a core loss of RM2.2 million in Q1 FY25.
RHB Research attributed the improvement to operating leverage from higher automotive project run rates and stronger industrial orders, which offset elevated input costs.
The group is targeting 20 per cent to 30 per cent revenue growth in FY26, with a net margin of four to six per cent, followed by another 10 per cent growth in FY27, excluding new project wins.
The automotive segment, which accounts for more than 60 per cent of revenue, is expected to remain the main earnings driver as delayed projects for a major customer are rolled out alongside a new US$25.9 million contract from Magna Autosystems.
RHB Research said full lamp assembly programmes for new Proton models based on the advanced modular architecture platform are expected to contribute RM50 million to RM55 million annually, while a second model slated for production in 2027 could add another RM15 million to RM20 million a year.
Automotive capacity utilisation remains healthy at about 80 per cent to 90 per cent. Although freight costs related to project transfer parts could temporarily weigh on margins, RHB Research expects efficiency gains to help offset the pressure.
New audio, video, navigation and infotainment assembly projects could also provide further upside.
Meanwhile, the semiconductor-focused sheet metal division remains the main driver of the industrial segment, with revenue expected to grow 15 per cent year on year and contribute RM7 million to RM10 million to FY26 earnings.
The division serves the back-end test equipment, instrumentation and hard disc drive industries, with client demand expected to remain strong through FY26 and into FY27.
RHB Research also expects industrial margins to widen as sheet metal capacity utilisation improves from the current 75 per cent to the 80 per cent range, alongside narrower losses or a turnaround in the die casting operations.
The group's new machine vision system assembly project for a China customer is also scaling up, with revenue expected to double from RM15 million in FY25.
RHB Research revised its FY26 to FY28 earnings forecasts by down 0.1 per cent, 14.4 per cent and 14.9 per cent, respectively, reflecting higher revenue growth assumptions but narrower margins for certain automotive projects.
Despite the earnings revisions, it raised its target price to RM0.64 from rolling forward its valuation base year to FY27.
The valuation remains pegged to 18 times price earnings, representing one standard deviation above JHM's five-year mean.
At current valuations, JHM trades at 17 times FY26 forecast earnings, or 13 times FY27 earnings, and 0.9 times FY26 book value, which RHB Research said leaves room for a valuation re-rating as earnings delivery improves.
Key downside risks include weaker demand, cost escalations, production delays and a weaker US dollar.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Aliff Syukri allowed to hold off apology to ex-minister Kadir pending appeal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court today allowed entrepreneur and social media personality Datuk Seri Aliff Syukri Kamaruzaman to defer an order requiring him to apologise to former Tourism Minister Tan Sri Abdul Kadir Sheikh Fadzir for defamation.
The decision was made pending the outcome of Aliff's appeal at the Court of Appeal.
Aliff's lawyer Mahmud Abdul Jumaat said the court also allowed his client's proposal for the
RM250,000 damages awarded
to be paid into Abdul Kadir's solicitors' stakeholder account pending the disposal of the appeal.
"The court also allowed the defendant's (Aliff) proposal for the RM250,000 damages awarded to be paid to Abdul Kadir's solicitors' stakeholder account pending the disposal of the appeal," he said after proceedings on the stay of execution before judge Roslan Mat Nor.
However, Aliff, 38, remains prohibited from publishing or causing to be published any statement that is the same as, or has a similar defamatory effect to, the statements made against Abdul Kadir, 86.
On April 29, Roslan, in allowing Abdul Kadir's suit, ordered Aliff to pay RM250,000 in damages over defamatory statements alleging unpaid investment debts amounting to millions of ringgit.
The court also ordered Aliff to pay RM50,000 in legal costs.
The court also granted Abdul Kadir's application for injunctions, ordering Aliff and his representatives to stop publishing the defamatory statements, remove them from all social media platforms within seven days and provide a written undertaking not to repeat them.
Roslan said Aliff had failed to provide a convincing explanation as to why he had no alternative means of recovering the alleged debt and instead resorted to making the libellous post that led to the suit.
On Sept 6, 2023, Abdul Kadir filed a RM70 million defamation suit against Aliff over alleged unpaid investment debts amounting to millions of ringgit.
Aliff had posted on his social media accounts demanding that the veteran politician pay a RM30 million investment for a joint venture project called Buckingham-By-The-Sea in Desaru, Johor.
Abdul Kadir testified that a doctored photograph depicting him with his eyes blacked out with ink, alongside a glass of wine, a bottle of alcohol and a woman, implied that he was a womaniser and an alcoholic.
He said the altered image, taken at an official function where he was the guest of honour, was intended to defame him and tarnish his reputation.
In his defence case summary, Aliff said he was personally and directly involved in a 2018 joint venture agreement involving Abdul Kadir and two companies, under which he had paid RM30 million as an investment.
He claimed the parties had agreed to investment returns but failed to honour the agreement, with Abdul Kadir aware of the alleged breaches.
Aliff also alleged that Abdul Kadir became difficult to contact and had refused, been careless or neglected to repay the money as promised, resulting in a debt owed to him and other parties to the agreement.

Title: Myanmar's Min Aung Hlaing heads to Russia for official visit, state media reports
Article:
NAYPYIDAW: Myanmar junta chief-turned-president Min Aung Hlaing left for Russia on Monday for his first official visit to the country since he assumed the presidency in April, according to state media.
Russia will be the fifth country Min Aung Hlaing has visited since becoming president, with official trips to India, China, Laos, and earlier this month, Thailand.
The former general is the subject of a raft of Western sanctions and has been on a quest for international legitimacy since winning a vote in parliament to become president, which came after an election dominated by an army-backed party in the absence of a viable opposition.
Min Aung Hlaing made four visits to Russia as junta chief, the first in June 2021 to attend a security conference, five months after seizing power in a coup.
He visited twice in 2022 and again in March 2025 when he held formal talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow.
Russia is hoping to open up opportunities in Myanmar for its energy companies.
The two countries signed an agreement to construct a small-scale nuclear power plant in Myanmar when Min Aung Hlaing met Putin in 2025.
Russia and Myanmar signed a memorandum on investment cooperation for the strategically located Dawei Special Economic Zone in February 2025, including the construction of a port and an oil refinery.
Min Aung Hlaing's latest trip includes a Myanmar-Russia business forum. Joining him will be the chief minister of the Tanintharyi region, where Dawei is located, and the head of Myanmar's aerospace agency, according to state media.
Defence ties have grown in recent years with Moscow providing army training and university scholarships to thousands of Myanmar soldiers, as well as selling arms to a military blacklisted by some Western countries.
Russia also earlier this year said it would help to train Myanmar's first cosmonaut.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Shein eyes company valuation of around US$25bil in Hong Kong IPO
Article:
HONG KONG: Online fast-fashion retailer Shein is eyeing a company valuation of around US$25 billion in its Hong Kong IPO, said three people with knowledge of the matter, down from nearly US$100 billion four years ago due to challenging business conditions.
Singapore-headquartered Shein, known for selling US$5 dresses and US$10 jeans to shoppers in about 160 countries, is aiming to launch its much-awaited initial public offering later this week, Reuters has reported.
One of the three sources said that the company, which was founded in China in 2012, was looking at a valuation of between US$25 billion and US$28 billion based on the marketing price band for the offering.
The sources declined to be named as they were not authorised to speak to the media ahead of a public announcement of the deal terms. A spokesperson for Shein did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
The latest company valuation target is also lower than US$30 billion-US$40 billion that Shein was aiming for at the beginning of this month and soon after it kickstarted investor meetings, Reuters reported on Aug 4.
Some investors, who attended IPO presentations or reviewed recent financial statements, have told Reuters they were not convinced Shein could return to the growth rates that valued it at US$98.20 billion in a 2022 fundraising round.
A lower valuation could weigh on Shein's financials as under the terms of its IPO filing, the company would be required to provide extra shares to certain pre-IPO investors if the valuation falls below agreed thresholds.

Title: Gold gains on weaker dollar, reduced Fed rate-hike bets
Article:
NEW YORK: Gold drifted higher on Monday, supported by a weaker dollar and recent soft economic data that reduced expectations for a US interest rate hike next month.
Spot gold rose 0.60 per cent to US$4,400.15 per ounce by 0710 GMT. Prices hit a more-than-two-month high last week.
US gold futures for December delivery edged 0.40 per cent higher to US$4,456.50.
The US dollar index was down 0.20 per cent, making greenback-priced metals more affordable for other currency holders.
"Gold has taken the ball and run with it to start the week, with soft inflation numbers keeping the US dollar under pressure and giving gold extra headroom to push towards the US$4,400 level," said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade.
"A sustained move above US$4,500 would likely need additional dollar weakness or a clearer pullback in energy prices."
An unexpected decline in US nonfarm payrolls in July, coupled with data showing only mild consumer price inflation, has reduced expectations that the US Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next month.
Traders are now pricing in a 29 per cent chance of a September rate hike, down from 47 per cent a month earlier, CME's FedWatch Tool showed.
Lower interest rates reduce the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, enhancing its appeal to investors.
Markets are now awaiting minutes of the Fed's July meeting, due on Wednesday, for further clues on policymakers' monetary stance.
On the geopolitical front, US President Donald Trump's envoys met with Egyptian, Qatari and Turkish mediators in Cairo on Sunday, a diplomatic source said, aiming to advance his Gaza peace plan, even as Israel pressed on with airstrikes in the enclave.
Among other metals, spot silver rose 1.80 per cent to US$65.82 per ounce. Platinum gained 0.70 per cent to US$1,759.69, while palladium climbed 1.70 per cent to US$1,334.77.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor shuts Kulai factory after Jalur Gemilang, state flag found upside down
Article:
KULAI: An industrial factory here has been temporarily closed after the Jalur Gemilang and Johor flag were found displayed upside down.
Johor Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the incident was being viewed seriously as both flags represented the identity, dignity and sovereignty of the country and state.
He said the incident could not be dismissed as a minor mistake or allowed to go without action.
"More so when two important symbols — the Jalur Gemilang and Johor flag — were found displayed upside down at the same premises," he said in a statement today.
The Kulai Municipal Council (MPKu) has temporarily closed the premises pending an explanation from the company and the completion of an undertaking, he said.
Both flags were immediately corrected.
Jafni said the Kulai district officer was also coordinating follow-up action with MPKu and relevant agencies to ensure appropriate action was taken under existing laws.
Police are investigating, while the company director will be called to give an explanation.
"If there is any breach of the law or applicable conditions, further action must be taken without fear or favour," he said.
Jafni said the local authority's action was based on the Licensing of Trades, Businesses and Industries By-Laws 2019, including By-law 49(2), which provides for the closure of premises, and By-law 45(1), concerning the flying of flags.
He warned all business owners, companies and industrial operators in Johor to ensure flags were displayed correctly, orderly and responsibly.
"Negligence cannot be used as an excuse to take lightly the respect due to symbols of national and state sovereignty," he said.
The state government, he said, would await the outcome of the investigation to determine the cause and those responsible.
"Our position is clear — the dignity of the country must be protected, the dignity of Johor must be upheld, flags must be respected and the law must be enforced," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fires near Greek capital controlled after claiming two lives
Article:
ATHENS: Two fires on the Greek island of Salamis near Athens that claimed two lives and led to the evacuation of nearly 600 people have been largely extinguished, the fire service said Monday.
"The situation is better, there is no active front," a fire department spokesman told AFP, adding that two helicopters and over 200 firefighters remained in the area.
The fires broke out Sunday near packed beaches in the south and east of the island just west of Athens that is popular with day travellers.
The evacuations were carried out by boat.
Though the civil protection agency quickly issued evacuation orders, the fire department said the fires spread in just seven minutes owing to strong winds, trapping an elderly couple near their home.
Three people remained hospitalised with burns on Monday.
After largely escaping the heatwave temperatures that blanketed much of Europe, Greece has been hit with several major wildfires since late July, fuelled by strong winds.
Thirty-six blazes have broken out over the past 24 hours around the country, according to the fire department.
Five firefighters have died so far, including a Danish pilot killed in a mid-air collision between two helicopters while battling a blaze near Athens earlier this month.

Title: Alam Damai house goes up in flames, Bomba suspect EV charging in foyer
Article:

Title: Ex‑JKR officer tells High Court Muhyiddin made no calls to help Nepturis in RM141m Jana Wibawa project
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — A former senior Public Works Department (JKR) officer today said he did not receive any phone calls from then prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin to help the contractor of a RM141 million government project, the High Court heard today.
Former Selangor JKR director Lokman Nasir, 62, said this while testifying as the 23rd prosecution witness in Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia president Muhyiddin’s power abuse and money laundering trial.
Lokman was in charge of supervising progress on the RM141 million project to build the Klang Utara district police headquarters (IPD), which was won by contractor Nepturis Sdn Bhd.
During cross-examination by Muhyiddin’s lawyer Chetan Jethwani, Lokman confirmed that there had been no interference from the Prime Minister’s Office while he was supervising the project, and that he did not meet with Muhyiddin.
Chetan: Didn’t receive calls from him or his office to help this contractor?
Lokman: No.
Previously, Nepturis Sdn Bhd’s hidden shareholder Lian Tan Chuan had, as the 21st prosecution witness, told the court that the company had won the RM141 million project on January 12, 2022, and that it had given its first-ever donation to a political party via a February 16, 2022 cheque for RM1 million to Bersatu as a “reward”.
Bank evidence showed that the RM1 million was deposited into Bersatu’s AmBank account on February 21, 2022, while Lian had last month said Nepturis had so far completed 98 per cent of the project.
Among other things, Lokman confirmed today that Nepturis had only started receiving interim payments from the government for progress on the RM141 million project in May 2022, and confirmed eight payment vouchers for over RM16 million paid to Nepturis from May 17, 2022 to February 3, 2023.
Lokman, who retired in April 2024, also agreed that there had been no discussions to terminate the RM141 million project during his tenure and also confirmed he did not know the latest status of the project.
Witness and former Selangor JKR director Lokman Nasir pictured at the Kuala Lumpur High Court on August 17, 2026. — Picture by Yusof Isa
Separately, JKR’s former quantity surveyors’ service director Datuk Zulkipeli Yamat, 63, testified today as the 24th prosecution witness in the trial
Zulkipeli said JKR had received proposal letters from the Finance Ministry to appoint contractors for each of the construction projects under the Jana Wibawa programme.
When asked by deputy public prosecutor Wan Nur Iman Wan Ahmad Afzal, Zulkipeli said only the Finance Ministry was involved in choosing these contractors, while JKR only waited for the letters from the Finance Ministry on the names of the contractors and projects.
He also confirmed that the Finance Ministry’s procurement division had a committee to evaluate contractors, which was chaired by Datin Rosni Mohd Yusoff and had four members (namely JKR’s representative Ruzimah Othman, two Finance Ministry representatives, and a Department of Irrigation and Drainage representative).
He said JKR’s role in that committee was to discuss contractors’ qualifications.
Confirming that four companies including Nepturis had been allowed to join the pre-qualification tender for the IPD Klang Utara project, Zulkipeli said it was up to the Finance Ministry to decide on how many companies are invited to join the tender project.
Witness and former JKR quantity surveying services director Datuk Zulkipeli Yamat pictured at the Kuala Lumpur High Court on August 17, 2026. — Picture by Yusof Isa
This morning, the prosecution amended the fourth power abuse charge that Muhyiddin is facing in this trial, by adding KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd.
Under the amended charge, Muhyiddin is accused of having abused his position as Bersatu president and then prime minister between March 1, 2020 and August 20, 2021 to obtain RM4.8m from Azman Yusoff and KCJ Engineering.
Muhyiddin pleaded not guilty when the amended charge was read out to him, before the trial continued.
In this trial, Muhyiddin is facing seven charges, namely four counts of alleged power abuse to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd), and three counts of alleged money laundering involving money that Bersatu received from Bukhary Equity.
The trial before High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin resumes tomorrow.
