Title: Sabah Heart Centre given top priority, Dzulkefly concedes staffing shortage remains a challenge
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 17 — Construction of the RM125 million Sabah Heart Centre is expected to begin in the third quarter of next year, with the facility targeted for completion and operation by the third quarter of 2029, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said today.
He said the project, approved under the 13th Malaysia Plan’s first rolling plan for 2026, is currently undergoing preliminary works, including the procurement of material testing services which are expected to be completed this month.
“If everything goes according to plan without disruption, we hope to start in the third quarter of 2027. With a 24-month or two-year construction period, the Sabah Heart Centre should be operational by the third quarter of 2029,” he told reporters today.
He was here chairing the first 2026 Joint Action Committee Meeting on Sabah Health Development with the state’s women, health and people’s wellbeing minister Datuk Julita Mojungki.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had announced the establishment of the heart centre in 2024 with at least three specialists to manage Sabah’s perennial health services shortage.
The project is among seven new health projects approved for Sabah under RMK-13 Rolling Plan 1, which has allocated RM1.57 billion for 53 health projects in the state, including 46 ongoing projects and seven new projects.
Dzulkefly said the Heart Centre would be given top priority by the Health Ministry, with the RM125 million allocation covering the overall project, including upgrading works, equipment procurement and related preliminary works.
It is understood that the current plan is to have the centre within the Queen Elizabeth II hospital, although it was previously reported that four hectares or 10 acres of land near University Malaysia Sabah had been identified and allocated for this purpose.
Asked whether the ministry would have enough specialists to staff the new centre when it opens, Dzulkefly acknowledged that human resources remained one of the ministry’s biggest longstanding challenges.
He said the ministry was working with the Public Service Department (JPA) to address shortages, including reducing bureaucratic delays in the appointment and placement of doctors.
“Human resources is my biggest legacy problem,” he said, adding that the ministry had now been given greater authority by JPA to manage the distribution of posts under its various service schemes.
He said several doctors were also currently undergoing specialist training and would eventually enter a period of supervised experience before being fully recognised as specialists.
“So, when the Sabah Heart Centre begins operations, I am confident we will be able to plan properly and increase the number of cardiology specialists,” he said.
The issue is particularly relevant to Sabah, where specialist services, including cardiology, remain limited and the National Heart Institute (IJN) Sabah currently has only one cardiologist serving the state, according to questions raised during the press conference.
Dzulkefly said the ministry would work to ensure the specialist pipeline was strengthened ahead of the centre’s opening.
Meanwhile, Dzulkefly also announced that the ministry opened up 607 new positions h in Sabah as of August 1, including 355 management and professional posts, comprising 77 specialist positions and 203 medical, dental and pharmacy officers, as well as 252 posts for the implementing group.
The ministry has also set a target for Sabah’s annual health allocation to increase by five per cent, with the allocation projected to reach RM4 billion by 2030.
Dzulkefly said these measures formed part of ongoing discussions between the Federal and Sabah governments on healthcare-related claims under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63), with five subcommittees examining issues including health autonomy, powers and authority, legal rights, overlapping jurisdictions, staffing, training, facilities and regulation.

Title: Ministry defends transfer of Sabah hospital director amid ongoing sexual harassment probe
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 17 — The Health Ministry’s decision to remove a Sabah hospital director from his post and transfer him to the state health department is pending further investigation into allegations of sexual harassment.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the administrative transfer was made deliberately to ensure the investigation could proceed without the officer remaining in a position that could potentially affect the process.
“We have made that decision consciously. We have conducted our internal investigation and there will be a full investigation thereafter,” he told reporters after chairing the first 2026 Joint Action Committee Meeting on Sabah Health Development here today.
His comments came after the hospital director’s lawyer, Joan Goh, said he was mulling taking legal action over the transfer.
The sexual harassment allegations were made by a subordinate working at the same hospital. It was also reported that there were at least two alleged “victims”, although this was not verified by authorities.
Dzulkefly said the officer had been placed at the Sabah Health Department as a medical officer, but stressed that the move did not constitute a demotion in terms of his service grade.
“We are only removing him from his role as hospital director so that he does not interfere with the investigation that will be conducted,” he said.
Dzulkefly said the ministry’s decision to transfer the officer was intended specifically to allow the investigative process to proceed without disruption.
He stressed that the administrative move did not alter the officer’s service grade, but removed him from his leadership position while the matter is being investigated.
Goh said that her client is challenging the transfer and has sought an explanation from the ministry over the reasons and evidence relied upon in making the decision.
Goh had reportedly submitted a formal representation to the ministry on behalf of her client, questioning the authority to remove him from his post before the conclusion of any disciplinary proceedings.
The case drew public attention last month after Kepayan assemblyman Chin Tek Ming and Parti Warisan’s Dr Istefan Koh brought the case to social media calling for a thorough investigation into allegations of sexual harassment and workplace bullying involving hospital staff.
Sabah Police Commissioner Datuk Jauteh Dikun confirmed that police had opened an investigation following a report lodged in January concerning allegations of sexual harassment involving a hospital director.
Jauteh had said the alleged incident was reported to have taken place in October last year.

Title: Road crashes cost Malaysia up to RM30b a year, but human cost of 18 daily deaths is far greater, says minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — Malaysia incurs up to RM30 billion in socio-economic losses each year due to road accidents, said Works Minister Dato Sri Alexander Nanta Linggi.
He said the figure was based on the economic value of the risks associated with fatalities, including loss of productivity and income, treatment costs, as well as the impact on families and society.
“However, despite all these calculations, the loss of life still cannot be valued in ringgit,” he said in a post on X today.
Nanta said the findings on the socio-economic impact of road accidents were presented at the Cabinet Committee on Road Safety and Congestion meeting chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
He said that last year alone, road accidents claimed 6,537 lives, equivalent to an average of 18 deaths a day.
Nanta said what was particularly worrying was that 80.6 per cent of accidents were attributed to human factors.
“This shows that road safety is not the responsibility of a single ministry alone. It requires a comprehensive approach encompassing education, enforcement, technology and safer infrastructure.
“In this regard, the Works Ministry’s (KKR) position is clear. We do not want to merely repair roads after accidents occur. We want to build and maintain safer roads that reduce risks and minimise human error,” he said.
Nanta added that the RM30 billion figure was more than an economic cost, as it reflected the wide-ranging impact of road tragedies on families and society.
“The greatest loss is the loss of loved ones. We must not regard 18 deaths a day as normal. Every life saved is a victory for the people,” he said. — Bernama

Title: O&G sevice provider Alam Maritim Resources says CEO Azmi Ahmad under MACC remand
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — Alam Maritim Resources Bhd today announced that its group managing director and group chief executive officer Datuk Azmi Ahmad is under remand to facilitate an ongoing investigation by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC).
The service provider to the oil and gas industry said the remand is for the purpose of facilitating the ongoing investigation and does not constitute any finding of wrongdoing.
“The board has taken the necessary measures to ensure continuity of the group’s operations and will make further announcements should there be any material development,” it said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia. — Bernama

Title: Sabah sets aside nearly RM1b to unlock state agriculture, industry and tourism potential
Article:
KENINGAU, Aug 17 — The Sabah State Government has allocated nearly RM1 billion for the development of the agricultural, industrial and tourism sectors which continue to be among the main drivers of Sabah’s economic growth this year.
In this regard, Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor wants district officers to look into the economic potential in their respective areas.
“There are districts that have strengths in agriculture. Some have tourism potential. Some have marine resources. Some also have potential in industry and trade. This potential needs to be identified and developed in a planned manner.
“Our task is to ensure that this potential can be translated into investment opportunities, jobs and increased income for the people,” he said at the opening ceremony of the 29th Sabah State District Officers’ Conference here today.
Hajiji sees the Blue Economy as an area that has great potential, especially in rural areas.
“Sabah has marine resources, biodiversity and vast coastal areas. This potential needs to be harnessed prudently to create new economic opportunities and increase the income of the community.
“I hope that the district officer can help identify the potential and facilitate investments that suit the needs and strengths of each district,” he said.
For this year, he said the state government has a development allocation ceiling of RM12.02 billion for 1,173 programmes and projects under the 13th Malaysia Plan, the highest in the history of the Sabah Budget.
“The allocation ceiling is for 241 extension projects while 932 are new projects, however, the larger the allocation provided, the greater our responsibility to ensure that their implementation is truly effective,” he said.
Therefore, the Chief Minister wants each district officer to pay serious attention to the implementation of projects and programmes in their respective districts and monitoring must be carried out continuously.
“If there is a problem, it must be identified early and if there is a delay, the cause must be known and appropriate action must be taken,” he added.
He said district and sub-district officers also need to change the way they view development success and not just look at the number of approved projects. — Bernama

Title: Royal death brings early closure to Kelantan Heritage Weapons Festival in Kota Bharu
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Aug 17 — The Kelantan Heritage Weapons Festival 2026 has been closed today following the death of a member of the Kelantan royal family.
The Sultan of Kelantan’s Media Office announced that all festivals and activities at the event, which was taking place from yesterday until September 5 at Istana Balai Besar here, had been postponed immediately.
“All festivals and activities are postponed immediately. The cooperation of all parties in this matter is greatly appreciated,” the statement said.
The closure follows the death of the aunt of the Sultan of Kelantan Sultan Muhammad V, Datuk Tengku Salwani Almarhum Sultan Yahya Petra, at 6.10 am this morning at the age of 82.
Confirmation of the death was made through the Sultan of Kelantan’s Office in a statement here today.
“Let us pray together that the deceased’s soul may be blessed by Allah SWT and placed with those who believe and do righteous deeds, and receive His forgiveness and blessings,” the statement said.
Tengku Salwani, who was born on August 26, 1944, is the daughter of Sultan Yahya Petra ibni Almarhum Sultan Ibrahim and the elder sister of the late Sultan Ismail Petra.
The festival, which features various traditional weapons, pitis and Kelantan heritage treasures that are full of historical, artistic and cultural value, runs from 9 am to 10 pm and admission is free.
Among the main attractions is a special exhibition of the Kelantan Sultanate Crown which is displayed to visitors for the first time, in addition to various activities such as songket weaving demonstrations, making kelingkam cloth, traditional performances and a Kelantan Malay Clothing workshop. — Bernama

Title: Baby Eden’s arrival makes Mahathir great‑grandfather, Ally Mukhriz celebrates newborn online
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 17 — A new chapter has begun in the storied Mahathir family, as Ally Mukhriz — daughter of Parti Pejuang Tanah Air president Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir — has given birth to her first child, a baby boy named Eden Zakaria Ezran Cheah.
Born on Sunday morning at 8.48am, weighing 2.9kg, Eden is not only Ally and her husband Ezran Daud Cheah’s first child, but also the very first great grandchild of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and his wife Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali.
Ally, whose full name is Meera Alyanna Mukhriz, shared the joyful news on Threads: “Ezran and I are happy to announce the birth of our baby boy, Eden Zakaria Ezran Cheah. Born 16.08.26 at 8.48am at 2.9kg. Thank you everyone for sending the well wishes and we hope to share more soon.”
Her mother, Tok Puan Norzieta Zakaria, echoed the family’s delight in a heartfelt Instagram post: “Assalamualaikum. Praise be to Allah. Our hearts are overflowing with love as we proudly welcome our precious grandson into the family. Welcome to the world, little one! You are already so deeply loved.”

Title: DOE: Air quality mostly moderate nationwide, Johan Setia stands out with unhealthy reading 137
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 17 — Johan Setia in Selangor recorded an Air Pollutant Index (API) of 137 at 1pm today, the only location nationwide to report unhealthy air quality, the Department of Environment (DOE) said in a statement.
Across the country, eight stations reported good levels and 58 stations at moderate. The DOE said it had intensified patrols and drone monitoring in Johan Setia but found no open burning. Ground checks also confirmed no such activity, with banners prohibiting burning installed as a preventive measure.
The DOE said overall inspections found conditions in Johan Setia were under control, with no open burning detected at the time.
According to the department, satellite data from the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) on August 16 detected 323 hotspots in Kalimantan, 61 in Sumatra and one in Pahang.
Regional haze maps showed moderate to dense smoke from clusters of hotspots in Kalimantan and lighter haze from central Sumatra, with several monitoring stations there recording unhealthy to hazardous levels.
The DOE said national action plans on open burning and haze had been activated to coordinate enforcement. Landowners are urged to monitor vulnerable areas such as landfills, peatlands, farms and plantations to prevent trespassing and fires.
The public is also reminded not to carry out open burning.
Under the Environmental Quality Act (Amendment) 2024, offenders face fines between RM25,000 and RM1 million, up to five years’ jail, or both. Compounds of up to 50 per cent of the maximum fine may also be imposed.
Hourly API readings are available at DOE’s
website
or via the MyJAS EQMS mobile app. The public may report open burning to the Fire and Rescue Department at 999 or the DOE hotline at 1-800-88-2727.

Title: Room to grow: 524 classroom projects worth RM668m in the works for 2027
Article:
KUALA NERUS, Aug 17 — A total of 524 additional classroom projects worth RM668 million are underway nationwide for the Year One intake in the 2027 session, said Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan.
Of these, 517 have been approved with Letters of Acceptance (LoAs), with three completed so far.
“The projects use modular methods and the Industrialised Building System,” he said after the handover of the first project completed ahead of schedule, from the Terengganu Public Works Department to the Education Ministry.
The handover was officiated by Minister Fadhlina Sidek at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Tok Jembal today.
The projects cover 459 schools and 1,780 classrooms, comprising 1,255 standard and 525 for the Special Education Integration Programme (PPKI).
He said Selangor topped the list with 143 projects, all of which have been approved. Kedah followed with 93 (92 approved), while Johor recorded 47 (45 approved).
“Terengganu has 45 projects and Penang 30, all with LoAs. Perak follows with 22, 18 of which have received LoAs.
Meanwhile, he said the projects in Pahang (50), Melaka (69), Kelantan (10), Perlis (8), Labuan (3), Kuala Lumpur (2) and Negeri Sembilan (2) have all been granted LoAs. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia Airlines pilots cleared in drug tests, MAG moves to cabin crew screening phase
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) has completed a mandatory drug screening for all Malaysia Airlines pilots, with every test returning negative, the company said in a statement today.
MAG said the exercise, concluded on August 15, covered all operationally active pilots.
The group will now begin screening approximately 2,840 Malaysia Airlines cabin crew, starting August 18 and targeted for completion by September 3.
Screening is also underway at sister airline Firefly.
As of August 15, more than half of its 158 pilots and 163 cabin crew had been tested, all with negative results. Firefly is expected to finish by August 25, ahead of the September 5 deadline set by the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM).
“The completion of this first phase is an important milestone in the measures we committed to implementing, but work does not stop here,” said Captain Nasaruddin A. Bakar, president and group chief executive officer of MAG.
“We are moving ahead with screening across other operational groups to ensure the same rigorous standards are applied consistently across our airlines.”
MAG also noted that it will maintain continuous random testing led by its Safety and Health team, alongside collaboration with the authorities.

Title: Pahang police investigate vandalised Bukit Tinggi temple statue, but no CCTV, no witnesses
Article:
KUANTAN, Aug 17 — Police have received three reports regarding the incident of a statue at a non-Muslim place of worship being vandalised in Bukit Tinggi, Bentong, yesterday.
Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the three police reports were made by a 49-year-old security guard, a 45-year-old monk and a 41-year-old man.
“The police have gone to the scene and initial investigations found that there were no closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras installed in the temple area and there were no independent witnesses who saw the incident,” he said in a statement today.
Meanwhile, Azry Akmar said his party viewed the incident seriously and investigations were still underway to identify the cause and the parties involved.
The case is being investigated under Section 295 of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
Police are investigating the desecration of statues of Hindu deities at the Brahmarishi Temple in Bukit Tinggi, Pahang believed to have taken place on August 16, 2026. — Picture from X/UpdateInfo
Meanwhile, he also advised the public not to speculate or spread information, especially via social media, which could affect the investigation or cause public concern.
“Any information regarding this incident should be channelled to the police to assist in the investigation,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Don’t just scrap UUCA, use it to reshape Malaysia’s universities, says UTM VC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — The repeal of the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) should not be seen as just the end of a law, but rather an opportunity to rebuild the country’s higher education ecosystem that is more mature, inclusive and forward-looking.
Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM) vice-chancellor Prof Dr Mohd Shafry Mohd Rahim said the change needed to be supported by a legal framework that could nurture knowledge, intellectual courage and creativity in line with technological, economic and geopolitical changes.
He said UTM welcomed the aspirations of the Ministry of Higher Education (KPT) to implement the transformation in a comprehensive and responsible manner.
“Today’s universities are not just places to impart knowledge, but also arenas for creating solutions, building ideas and developing citizens who are able to think independently and act ethically.
“Therefore, higher education legislation must evolve in line with changing times, without neglecting institutional stability and public interest,” he said in a statement.
Mohd Shafry said institutional autonomy should be the basis for the reform, with universities given sufficient space to determine academic priorities, strengthen research, develop talent and build strategic collaborations based on their respective strengths.
However, he said autonomy is not unlimited freedom, but rather needs to move in line with accountability, transparency, integrity and social responsibility.
Meanwhile, he said academic freedom needs to be strengthened as the heart of a credible university, with academics and students given space to explore difficult questions, present evidence-based views and disagree in a civilised manner.
“However, this freedom requires intellectual discipline. Arguments must be supported by facts, research must be ethical and discourse cannot be used as an excuse to spread extremist views or denigrate human dignity,” he said.
He said the new higher education legal framework also needs to recognise the diversity of institutions including universities, university colleges, technical-focused institutions and private education providers that have different mandates and challenges.
“The process of drafting a replacement framework must be consultative and evidence-based. The views of students, academics, administrators, alumni, industry, civil society and legal experts must be heard openly.
“The aim is not simply to change the name of an act, but to produce a regulation that is clearer, fairer and more resilient to future changes,” he said.
Mohd Shafry said UTM was prepared to contribute its expertise and work with the government and all stakeholders to ensure that the reform provides real benefits to students, institutions and the country.
According to him, the success of the abolition of AUKU should not be measured solely based on the date the act was repealed or new laws were passed, but rather through the ability of universities to be more courageous in seeking the truth, efficient in managing trust, open to celebrating differences and close to the needs of the people.
“This is an opportunity to build higher education that is not only competitive on the global stage, but also strong in its human values in line with the aspirations of the Malaysian Higher Education Plan (RPTM) 2026-2035,” he said.
On August 15, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government had given an assurance that AUKU would be abolished to provide greater freedom and democratic space for the student movement in this country. — Bernama

Title: UUCA repeal can give Malaysian universities room to compete globally, says local varsitities
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — The country’s new higher education legal framework must provide a conducive environment for Malaysian universities to grow, remain competitive and achieve excellence on par with leading institutions worldwide.
International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) Rector Professor Emeritus Datuk Seri Dr Osman Bakar said the framework should be progressive, fair and forward-looking, while safeguarding the sustainability and integrity of universities.
He said the move to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) presented an important opportunity to establish such a framework and empower universities to respond to the changing demands of an increasingly dynamic higher education landscape.
“IIUM views this move as an important development in renewing the country’s higher education landscape, particularly by creating greater space for student participation and voices, strengthening academic freedom, and enabling universities to continue serving as platforms for knowledge, thought and research,” he said in a statement today.
Osman also welcomed the Ministry of Higher Education’s commitment to conducting an inclusive engagement process with stakeholders across the higher education ecosystem, including university leaders, academics and students.
He said broad-based engagement was crucial to ensuring the new legal framework reflected the aspirations, realities and current needs of Malaysia’s higher education community.
Meanwhile, Universiti Malaysia Kelantan (UMK) Vice-Chancellor Professor Datuk Dr Arham Abdullah said the new legislation presented an opportunity to strengthen the governance and autonomy of higher education institutions in a more structured manner, including in asset and facilities management, income generation and strategic partnerships.
He said autonomy aligned with good governance and accountability principles could help universities optimise existing assets and facilities to generate income, while strengthening institutional development and student welfare.
Arham said appropriate autonomy could also enhance universities’ ability to establish strategic partnerships with the private sector and industry players, subject to the required approvals and financial and governance procedures.
“Such an approach is important to ensure universities can explore new opportunities without compromising accountability, transparency and the public interest,” he said.
Yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim assured that the government would repeal AUKU completely without introducing any new legislation that would restrict or suppress student movements.
AUKU has undergone seven rounds of amendments since it was introduced in 1971, including a 2012 amendment allowing students to participate in political party activities outside campus.
The latest amendment, in 2024, removed disciplinary action against students at public universities from the Vice-Chancellor’s jurisdiction. Such matters are now decided by the Student Disciplinary Committee following amendments to Section 16B of AUKU. — Bernama

Title: Future of Likas Wetlands, one of world’s only two city mangrove Ramsar sites, hangs in balance with mega project next door
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 17 — The Likas Wetlands – only two of its kind in the world located within a city and enjoys global Ramsar status – may cease to exist within 15 years if nothing is done to prevent polluted water from a nearby mega project infiltrating the 24-hectare gazetted site and killing the vegetation.
Sabah Wetland Conservation Society President, Datuk Zainie Abdul Aucasa who sounded the alarm bell was apparently referring to massive development coming up in the vicinity near Hakka Hall in Likas.
Speaking at the World Mangrove Day celebration, he cited its own Consultant’s Report at the event and hoped the Society would not have to resort to taking the authorities to court like in 2015 when they “approved a 31-storey condominium just outside our wetlands”.
The verdict was later overturned by the High Court on grounds of no Locus Standi (no right to sue).
Zaini said the Society would not waver or fail from its commitment to preserving the mangroves in the KK wetlands and defending its Ramsar status, the wetlands equivalent of World Heritage site.
“Together with our Consultant, my team and others went to see the relevant Minister, including the Chief Minister, who was very accommodating and even suggested that we form a Task Force.
“But I am still waiting for the first meeting. We have also met with the Mayor,” Zainie said.
“We have been very busy writing to all the relevant ministries. We wrote to the Ministry of Tourism, to all the agencies under the Ministry, EPD (Environmental Protection Department).
“Wildlife (Sabah Wildlife Department) and of course DBKK, attaching the Consultant’s Report of the threat the Ramsar site is facing (because of the latest project).”
“We want everybody’s support,” Zainie said, citing the distinction of Kota Kinabalu Wetlands being one of only two city mangrove Ramsar Sites in the world, the other being the 40-ha Yatsu-Higata Ramsar Site tidal flat in Chiba, Tokyo.
However, the KK Ramsar site comes out way ahead for being located directly within the city centre and featuring a much higher density of towering mangrove trees and fauna.
Mayor Dato’ Sri Dr Hj Subdin Samitah said: “The mangroves are an essential part of our coastal environment, its presence reminds us that the growth of a city must go hand in hand with the protection of its natural environment, but their protection cannot be achieved by any single organisation.”
He was represented by Ms Syron Tunggolou, Director of City Environmental Health Department, DBKK.
A large group of UMS students planted mangroves afterwards, UMS Forestry lecturer, Dr B Ahmad, SWCS deputy President, Rizal Ahmad, Organising Chairperson Renee Chin, Sabah Society Chairman Edwin Liew, WWF rep Ms Tan Hui Shim and sponsors from Borenos were present.

Title: DAP delegates have spoken, respect their decision, Kon Yeow tells Rafizi over unity govt stance
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 17 — DAP central executive committee member Chow Kon Yeow today told Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli to respect the party and its delegates’ decision to remain in the unity government.
Chow said this was a basic principle following Rafizi’s comments on the resolution adopted at DAP’s congress yesterday.
“We ask Rafizi to respect DAP and the decision of its delegates. That is the basic thing to do, isn’t it?” he told reporters after launching the public participation programme for the Draft Penang Structure Plan 2040 here.
Yesterday, Bersama leader Rafizi was reported saying that DAP’s decision to remain in the unity government was expected, claiming it was difficult for any political party that had “enjoyed” power to simply give it up.
Asked about claims that attendance at the DAP congress was below 50 per cent, Chow said the gathering remained valid as it had met the party’s quorum requirement.
He said at least 25 per cent of eligible delegates were required for the congress to proceed.
“We had more than 50 per cent and met the quorum requirement,” he said.
“Attendance at party elections is usually around 60 to 70 per cent, while voter turnout in a general election does not necessarily reach the full number either.
“So, does that mean our general election is invalid because only 65 per cent came out to vote? No,” he added.
On Rafizi’s remarks that Penang’s limited land supply had affected state revenue compared with states such as Johor, Chow said the state government had always planned for land development.
He said land acquisition and the opening up of land for development were ongoing for various purposes, including industrial use.
“The reclassification of rural areas as urban areas is also one method of rezoning land use in Penang,” he said.
“The state government maximises the use of existing land to ensure that development delivers the greatest impact for the state, taking into account Penang’s strengths and constraints,” he added.

Title: Penang’s undersea tunnel still on the map, draft plan keeps idea alive for 2040
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 17 — The proposed undersea tunnel or third bridge linking Penang island to the mainland was included as an indicative proposal in the Draft Penang State Structure Plan 2040 (RSN Penang 2040), Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said today.
He said the project remain in the draft plan as the agreement with the appointed company is still valid, although its eventual implementation would depend on development schedules.
“They are still there. The agreement is still valid and we have already awarded the tender to the company,” he told reporters after launching the publicity and public participation programme for the draft plan.
“Like many development areas and zones, they are shown only indicatively,” he said.
The third link, categorised as either an undersea tunnel or a bridge, was indicated in the draft plan as connecting Gurney Drive on the island to Bagan Ajam on the mainland.
He said the development areas and projects in the draft plan are indicative only as the implementation depends on the government of the day or sometimes, on the private sector in accordance with the designated development-control zones.
He said the draft RSN Penang 2040 should serve as a “compass” for the state’s development.
He said the draft plan gives clear direction on how Penang is developed, preserved and handed down to future generations.
“What we plan today will determine the face of Penang in 2040 and the generations after it, because Penang 2040 is not merely the state government’s vision; it is our shared future,” he said.
Chow also urged government departments and agencies to submit proposals for approved major projects to be included in the draft structure plan.
“It is important for us to include any proposal at the respective departmental level if approval has already been granted by the ministry to implement certain projects, especially major projects,” he said in his speech earlier.
“Provide this input during these public hearing sessions so that we can include these projects in RSN 2040,” he said.
“If there are plans that cannot be included, then when they are implemented, they will raise question marks among stakeholders, including the media, who will ask why this proposal is not in the RSN or in the local plan, for example,” he added.
Chow stressed that the draft was not a final or flawless document, and said the public could examine it, give feedback, submit proposals and challenge suggestions based on facts and public interest.
On Pulau Jerejak, he said the island is also included in the draft plan, but stressed that most of its land remains designated as a permanent forest reserve.
He said more than 80 acres of privately owned land are involved in the development proposals previously announced, while projects within the permanent forest reserve could only be considered for utilities or infrastructure.
“What was announced involves privately owned land, not the permanent forest reserve on Pulau Jerejak,” he said.
Asked whether the plan considered earthquake resilience and other disasters, Chow said disaster-related concerns had been given attention in the policies and development strategies proposed for the future.
Meanwhile, PLANMalaysia director-general Datuk Alias Rameli said the RSN Penang 2040 study was fully supported by a RM2 million allocation under the Fifth Rolling Plan of the 12th Malaysia Plan, with funding to continue under the First Rolling Plan of the 13th Malaysia Plan.
He said the study was completed over 12 months, from April 2025 to April 2026.
The public participation programme will run for four weeks until September 19.
The draft will be available for inspection at PLANMalaysia Penang in Komtar, the Seberang Perai City Council, five District and Land Offices, and online through the e-Publicity 2.0 platform on PLANMalaysia Penang’s official website.
Alias said the RSN is an official legal document under the Town and Country Planning Act 1976 that will guide major policies and proposals involving land use, the economy and the environment once gazetted.
“We understand that development must take place. It must be sustainable, and we must blend and balance the needs of economic growth, environmental preservation, and social inclusivity,” he said.

Title: Ranau court fines duo RM3,500 each after Sabah police link their wrist marks to illegal militant Philippine group
Article:
RANAU, Aug 17 — Two men were each fined RM3,500 by the Ranau Magistrate’s Court for being members of a Philippine organisation deemed illegal under the Societies Act 1966 – the latest in such cases in the district.
Roy Martin, 35, a farmer, and Mohd Sharin Ibrahim, 40, a tyre mechanic, were charged under Section 43 of the Societies Act 1966 for being members of Kappa Rho Kappa (KRK), also referred to in the investigation as the Knights of the Right Keppers, a Philippines-based militant organisation.
The court imposed a fine of RM3,500 on each accused, with six months’ imprisonment in default of payment.
The cases stemmed from a police operation conducted on June 5, 2026, at about 10.50am at HH Rich, Kg Kinasaraban, Ranau, under Op Tik Tok (Gangsterism).
More than an on-ground activation, Hotlink Prepaid Pasti Mampu Belanja Makan celebrated the spirit of Sabah's Geng Bijak Berbajet, people who know that spending wisely doesn't mean settling for less, but finding smarter ways to enjoy more.
According to the case documents, a team from the D7 Criminal Investigation Department (JSJ) of the Sabah Police Contingent Headquarters, led by Insp Jesmera bin Bandong, conducted checks on the two men at the premises.
During the inspection, police reportedly discovered three cigarette-burn marks on the upper part of the men’s right wrists, which investigators suspected to be associated with KRK membership.
Police also seized two mobile phones – a blue Redmi belonging to one of the men and an orange Realme phone belonging to the other – which were found to contain videos allegedly displaying content associated with the group.
The investigation subsequently sought verification from a gang-related crime expert, who confirmed that one of the accused was believed to be a member of the group based on the identifying marks found on his wrist.
Further checks with the Registrar of Societies Malaysia (ROS) Sabah also established that Kappa Rho Kappa (KRK) was not legally registered with the department. — Daily Express

Title: No water for nearly two months, then a RM120,000 bill — Putatan  condo dwellers ask why pay for water Sabah water utility was already treating
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 17 — Residents of Kingfisher Putatan Condominium (KFP) are refusing to pay the more than RM120,000 bill for water delivered by privately-operated tankers when they endured 55 days without supply between April and May.
Some said they had no choice but to purchase bottled water for drinking, washing, cooking, cleaning and other daily needs. They said the extra expenses should not have been necessary if the State Water Department (JANS) had fulfilled its responsibility.
Despite being located just south of Kota Kinabalu, Putatan has faced repeated water shortages since 2018. During the disruption, the condominium’s developer and management, Hap Seng Land Development and JCA Sdn Bhd, were compelled to procure water from private tankers.
However, residents later discovered that the water delivered was treated water originating from JANS itself; the same supply that had failed to reach them through the normal distribution network.
More than an on-ground activation, Hotlink Prepaid Pasti Mampu Belanja Makan celebrated the spirit of Sabah’s Geng Bijak Berbajet, people who know that spending wisely doesn’t mean settling for less, but finding smarter ways to enjoy more.
This emergency procurement drove costs up significantly, with residents charged RM7.50 per cubic metre after deducting the standard tariff of RM1.30 per cubic metre.
Many residents have refused to settle the outstanding bill, arguing they should not bear the financial burden of failures in the public water distribution system.
“The water we paid for was not from an alternative utility. It was JANS-treated water, only transported at higher logistical costs,” one resident said, questioning why consumers should be penalised for systemic shortcomings.
The crisis has left residents frustrated, with repeated interruptions continuing to affect sanitation, hygiene, cooking and daily living. The situation raised concerns that prolonged disruptions could escalate into a public health issue if not urgently addressed.
They are calling for accountability from the authorities, stressing that the government, as the primary duty-bearer, must ensure reliable access to clean water and sanitation.
After all, the government is legally and ethically responsible for ensuring clean water and sanitation infrastructure, although accountability is shared across multiple levels, including state agencies, utility operators, and regulatory bodies.
They are calling on the authorities to take concrete action to avoid legal intervention. Such a basic need and right for citizens, they argue, has been neglected. — Daily Express

Title: Century‑old Penang Hill railway gets track and roof repairs in scheduled January 2027 break
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 17 — Penang Hill’s iconic funicular will take a short break from January 4 to 10, 2027 for its scheduled bi annual maintenance, Penang Hill Corporation (PHC) announced today. Service is set to resume on January 11.
Engineers from Swiss manufacturer Garaventa AG will oversee the works, which include repairs to the Lower Station track structure, as well as upgrades to the funicular’s air conditioning system and roof. PHC said the shutdown is part of routine safety checks designed to keep the hill’s century old railway running smoothly.
During the closure, visitors can use the jeep service operated by the Penang Hill Jeep Service Association near the Penang Botanic Gardens Department Office, or take existing hiking routes to the summit.

Title: Sarawak forest fire in Daro enters eighth day, 4ha still burning
Article:
DARO, Aug 17 — Firefighters are on their eighth day of working to extinguish a forest fire in Kampung Kut here, which has affected about 29ha of land.
The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) said in a statement that firefighters are working to completely extinguish the remaining hotspots of the forest fire.
About 4ha of the affected area remained unextinguished as of Sunday.
Firefighters from the Daro fire station were deployed to three sectors during the operation.
“Sector one is located behind a petrol station, sector two along the main road, while sector three is near a telecommunications tower,” said Bomba.
Firefighting operations continued until 5pm, with two excavators deployed to create firebreaks to prevent the blaze from spreading further.
Firefighters also used water from nearby drains and a check dam to support suppression efforts.
A distress call on the fire was first received at around 1.40pm on Aug 10. — The Borneo Post

Title: Kuching man loses RM104,310 after falling for WhatsApp scam from friend’s hijacked account
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 17 — A 49-year-old man here lost RM104,310 to a phone scam last week.
Kuching police chief ACP Alexson Naga Chabu said the victim was contacted via WhatsApp from a friend’s number, but it turned out the account had been hacked and hijacked.
“Last Thursday when the victim was in his office, he received a message from the number that belonged to his friend seeking help to make payments for the purchase of an item.
“Having trusted the message, the victim then made four transfers to three different accounts from Aug 13 to Aug 15, amounting to a total sum of RM104,310.
“On Aug 15, he was informed by his friend that the WhatsApp account was believed to have been hacked, saying he did not request the victim to make such transfers,” Alexson said in a statement.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating and dishonestly inducing the delivery of property.
The Section provides for imprisonment of up to 10 years, caning, and a fine upon conviction.
Alexson reminded the public to be vigilant against such scam tactics by ceasing any suspicious correspondences immediately, not providing any personal or banking information to unknown individuals, and to contact the nearest police station to conduct checks or lodge a report.
“Members of the public are advised to conduct prior checks before making payments to a third party and to check suspicious accounts and phone numbers via the Semak Mule PDRM link at https://semakmule.rmp.gov.my,” he added. — The Borneo Post

Title: Johor businessman’s body bound in net, dumped in river; four accused face murder charge
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Aug 17 — Four men were charged at the Magistrate’s Court here with murdering a businessman, whose body was bound and covered in a net before being found in a river earlier this month.
The accused — S. Yogesvaran, 40; Lim Yong Ming, 26; N. Achutan, 32; and How Han Wei, 33 — nodded to indicate they understood the charge after it was read before Magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno in Bahasa Melayu.
However, no plea was recorded as cases under Section 302 of the Penal Code fall under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
According to the charge, the men were accused of murdering Low Kai Xian, 39, between 2.35pm on July 29 in front of the Sinhai Sdn Bhd restaurant in Jalan Emas Putih 2, Taman Sri Skudai, Johor Bahru, and 12.30pm on August 3 in Sungai Tanjung Sembrong here.
The charge was framed under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which provides for the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years and, if the death penalty is not imposed, whipping of not less than 12 strokes upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Nur Shahzleen Ibrahim appeared for the prosecution, while Yogesvaran, Yong Ming and Han Wei were represented by counsel S.J. Sean Dudley. Achutan was represented by his counsel Datin Freda Sabapathy.
Present for a watching brief during the proceedings were lawyers, Chuan Shyie Chien and Kenji Soh Xin Da, who were representing the victim’s family.
The court set October 14 for mention and the submission of the autopsy and deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) reports. This is in addition to submitting the closed-circuit television (CCTV) and mobile phone forensics.
Previously, it was reported that police arrested five suspects following the discovery of a 39-year-old businessman’s body floating in Sungai Tanjung Sembrong, Parit Raja, earlier this month.
The body, believed to be dumped in the river, was found bound and covered in a net, by the nearby residents.
Investigators also found five rocks placed with the victim’s body to weigh down the remains and prevent the body from surfacing.
The victim was later identified as a Johor Bahru-based businessman from Iskandar Puteri and had been reported missing since July 29.
He was identified by his next of kin based on his clothing and personal belongings.
Police said the motive for the murder may have been linked to debt.

Title: Pantai firefighters extinguish blaze on Jalan Kerinchi, BMW destroyed, Axia 30 per cent damaged
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — A BMW was destroyed and a Perodua Axia partially damaged after a blaze broke out at KL Gateway Mall, Jalan Kerinchi, last night.
The Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department said it received an emergency call via the NG999 line at 9.53pm before dispatching six firefighters from the Pantai station to the scene,
New Straits Times
reported.
Operations commander Mokhtar Ramli said firefighters found two vehicles at the scene — the BMW was completely gutted, while the Perodua Axia sustained about 30 per cent damage.
The fire was brought under control and extinguished. The cause is under investigation.

Title: Sarawak air quality improves as Serian and Samarahan drop from unhealthy to moderate
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 17 — Sarawak recorded moderate air quality at all monitoring stations except Bario, where the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading remained at good level as of 8am on Monday, according to the Natural Resources and Environment Board’s Daily Haze Watch.
Air quality in Serian and Samarahan improved from unhealthy levels — with API readings of 157 and 151 respectively at 4pm on Sunday — to moderate levels of 98 and 92 by 8am.
Lundu and Tebedu also improved, dropping from unhealthy readings of 111 and 109 at 4pm on Sunday to 93 and 73 respectively by 8am.
However, three areas recorded slight increases in API readings. They were Sibu, rising from 66 at 4pm on Sunday to 70 by 8am; Kapit (from 52 to 54); and Lubok Antu (from 68 to 70).
Samalaju registered the biggest drop, from 79 at 4pm on Sunday to 62 by 8am, followed by Miri (from 79 to 65), Industrial Training Institute Miri (from 75 to 62), Limbang (from 68 to 52).
Kuching’s API reading also fell further to 87 by 8am, seven points lower than 4pm on Sunday.
Other locations with decreasing readings were Sri Aman, from 84 at 4pm on Sunday to 80 by 8am; Sarikei (from 76 to 75); Bintulu (from 70 to 67); Mukah (from 59 to 57).
Lawas remained unchanged at 67, while Bario’s recorded 50.
An API reading ranging from 51 to 100 is classified as moderate, while API readings between 0 and 50 are categorised as good. — The Borneo Post

Title: Man, 35, dies after motorcycle strikes lorry left without fuel on Tumpat flyover
Article:
TUMPAT, Aug 17 — A 35-year-old motorcyclist was killed when his Yamaha 135LC struck the rear of a parked lorry on the Wakaf Bharu flyover here yesterday evening.
The accident happened at about 5pm as the victim was riding from Kota Bharu towards Pengkalan Kubor,
Berita Harian
(BH) reported.
Tumpat district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Khairi Shafie said the lorry had been left on the left shoulder of the flyover after running out of fuel. The victim was believed to have collided with its right rear section while negotiating a bend.
He told BH that the man suffered severe chest injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene by a medical assistant. The body was later sent to Tumpat Hospital for a post mortem, which confirmed the cause of death as multiple fatal injuries sustained in the crash.
Police are investigating the case under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Members of the public with information are urged to contact the Tumpat district traffic investigation officer at 09 7257222 or visit the district traffic office.

Title: Religious leaders launch Tabung Haji RCI outreach, clarify misuse risks and safeguard 9.7 million depositors’ savings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — Efforts to explain the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) will be extended nationwide to help the public gain a comprehensive understanding of how the institution’s deposits were managed.
Former Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Datuk Seri Dr Mujahid Yusof Rawa said the initiative would see Islamic scholars and religious figures explaining the RCI TH findings through mosques, surau, schools, government departments, colleges, universities and community education platforms.
He said the initiative followed a special conference, Hifz al-Mal, which brought together more than 100 scholars and religious leaders from across the country yesterday to discuss the findings and the responsibility of safeguarding the savings of 9.7 million depositors.
“The objective is clear: the facts must be explained, the trust must be upheld, and the misuse of the people’s assets must not be allowed to happen again. Tabung Haji is a trust held on behalf of the Muslim community. Protecting it is our shared responsibility,” he said in a Facebook post.
Mujahid, who is also Amanah deputy president, said the Malaysian Ulama Secretariat organised the conference at De Palma Hotel in Ampang in collaboration with Malaysian Ulama Council Mursyid al-’Am (Spiritual Leader) Abdul Rahim Abdul Rahman.
“What makes the conference particularly significant is that it brought together religious figures alongside professionals and scholars from various fields, including chartered accountants, economic commentators, legal practitioners, religious educators and pondok scholars.
“This combination of expertise allows a more comprehensive discussion of the RCI findings on Tabung Haji, covering religious, financial, economic, accounting, legal and governance aspects, as well as the responsibility of safeguarding the community’s assets,” he said.
Among the main sessions was an examination of the RCI findings from a professional perspective, as well as the roles of religious figures and the community in understanding and safeguarding the trust placed in them.
Mujahid said the conference was founded on the principle of Hifz al-Mal, or the protection of wealth, particularly given TH’s role in managing the savings of millions of Muslims to fund their haj pilgrimage. — Bernama
